Hi Evan / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great to meet the two of you and walk through Acme's realtime assistant use case. Below is a concise recap of what we discussed and the open items I promised to follow up on.

Recap (agreed high-level requirements):
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile end-to-end response time <= 250ms for single-turn assistant responses (streaming enabled).
- Throughput: Target sustained throughput ~250 req/s during business hours; peak bursts up to ~400 req/s for scheduled campaigns.
- Concurrency: ~35-50 parallel in-flight requests per downstream worker (connection pooling). Overall concurrency target for phase 1: ~300 concurrent requests across the service.
- Streaming: Token streaming required for first-token <120ms when model has <256 prompt tokens. We also expect chunked client consumption (server-sent events / chunked HTTP).

Open items I will follow up on:
1) Confirm per-worker vs org-wide concurrency model you prefer (you mentioned connection pooling on each app server).
2) Provide Redwood’s hosted baseline rate limits and a suggested Dedicated capacity quote that matches your throughput/concurrency requirements.
3) Share a short SOC2 summary and our standard security artifacts.

Attachments: Acme mutual action plan (acme-ma-plan-v1.pdf) — I’ve attached the MA plan and will iterate after we lock the concurrency numbers.

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive w/ our infra engineer (Laura) to validate streaming behavior and network egress shaping — can you do Fri 8/27 10–11am PT?
- I’ll send a preliminary concurrency/throughput quote by EOD Thu (8/26).

If anything above looks off, please flag and I’ll update.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency model: We use connection pooling on each app server; each worker will typically keep 20–40 concurrent requests open to the model service. The 35–50 number you listed per worker is in the right ballpark.
- Org-wide concurrency: For phase 1 we expect ~300 concurrent requests aggregated across all workers; if we run simultaneous campaigns that could spike toward ~500 for short periods.
- Throughput: Our 250 req/s is the average we expect; campaigns create short bursts that can reach 350–400 req/s for 2–5 minutes.
- Streaming: Important for our UX — we need the first token within ~100–150ms for short prompts. We do partial rendering as tokens arrive.

Action items for us:
- Please include per-minute and per-second burst behavior in the proposal (how Redwood handles short spikes).
- Can you confirm whether hosted rate limits are per-API-key or per-account? We may prefer per-key limits for service isolation.

Also — we'll need SOC2 summary and any IP/data handling notes in the packet. Looking forward to Friday’s deep-dive.

—Evan

Evan — thanks, good points. Quick clarifications and what we can offer based on your targets: 

1) Hosted baseline limits (typical):
- Request rate: 120 req/s sustained per account, with burst handling up to ~240 req/s for short periods (≈ 60s).
- Concurrent connections: default soft limit 20 concurrent requests per API key; can be raised with account-level quota adjustments.
- Token throughput: default 100k tokens/minute, adjustable for enterprise customers.

Note: these are defaults for our hosted offering. Because your expected sustained throughput (250 req/s) and concurrency (~300) exceed hosted defaults, we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a hosted enterprise quota bump.

2) Dedicated / Reserved capacity proposal (prelim):
- Reserved concurrent inference slots: 400 (covers sustained 250 req/s + headroom for spikes up to 400 req/s).
- Connection pooling guidance: recommend allowing 30–40 concurrent connections per worker and using a local connection pooler to reuse keep-alive TCP connections.
- Burst policy: Dedicated pools support autoscale buffer that handles short spikes up to 1.5x reserved capacity for up to 120s before shedding/policy-based fallback.
- Streaming behavior: Dedicated supports immediate token streaming; our infra tuning can meet first-token latency targets around ~100–150ms under normal network conditions for models with <256 prompt tokens.

3) Rate-limit granularity: Hosted limits are enforced per-account by default; we can create per-API-key quotas for isolation and have customer-side routing policies to map service keys to different quota buckets.

4) Next steps and deliverables I’ll send by EOD Thu (8/26):
- Preliminary Dedicated capacity quote spreadsheet (redwood-dedicated-concurrency-quote.xlsx).
- SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).
- Updated MA plan reflecting concurrency figures (attached).

Technical deep-dive: Laura will run the session Friday 8/27 10–11am PT. Joining details (calendar invite) to follow.

If you want a smaller hosted trial first we can also provision an elevated hosted quota for 2 weeks to validate latency/streaming before committing to Dedicated.

Best,
